sandhi.note: A final n stays before m; the words are only written together.
Visarga before c becomes ś (गजारूढश्चामरः); before t it becomes s (चामरस्त्रिदश…).
a + ā → ā. The same rule joins त्रिदश + अर्दन.

samasa.alt: Also read as a saptamī tatpuruṣa, गजे आरूढः ‘seated on an elephant’; आरूढ (आ + √रुह्) is transitive, so the accusative analysis fits the participle better.

samasa.sense: tormentor of the gods (त्रिदश ‘the Thirty’, a round name for the gods)

morph.note: Locative absolute (sati saptamī): participle and noun in the locative, ‘he having been slain’ — the time of the main action.
Perfect of √गम्: reduplication ज- (g → j) and the root shortened to -ग्म- in weak forms; in the strong 3rd singular -गाम (आ-ज-गाम).

mantras.anvaya: महिषस्य तस्मिन् महावीर्ये चमूपतौ हते (सति), गजारूढः त्रिदशार्दनः चामरः आजगाम।
mantras.anvaya_en: A locative absolute (हते … चमूपतौ) sets the time; the main clause has the subject with two epithets and the verb आजगाम.
mantras.lit: That mighty commander of Mahiṣa having been slain, Cāmara, tormentor of the gods, came, mounted on an elephant.
mantras.tr: When Mahiṣa’s mighty general had fallen, Cāmara, the scourge of the gods, came forward on an elephant.

comm.t: The second general. Cāmara was named among the commanders at 2.41 (युयुधे चामरः); his epithet त्रिदशार्दनः was used of the whole asura host at 2.60.

sandhi.note: The prefix निस् keeps its sibilant before p and it becomes ṣ after i: निः + प्रभा → निष्प्रभा.

samasa.type: tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa (हुंकार = हुम् इति कारः, the utterance of ‘hum’)
samasa.sense: beaten down by her cry alone

morph.note: Perfect of √मुच्: reduplication मु- and guṇa u → o (मु-मोच).
Periphrastic perfect: the causative stem पातय- with -आम् and the perfect of √अस् (आस). Causatives form their perfect this way: ‘caused (it) to fall’.
The genitive marks the person aimed at, where 3.9 used the locative (भद्रकाल्याम्); a usage found in epic narrative.

mantras.anvaya: अथ सः अपि देव्याः शक्तिं मुमोच। अम्बिका तां (शक्तिं) द्रुतं हुंकाराभिहतां निष्प्रभां भूमौ पातयामास।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two sentences. In the second, ताम् carries two predicative adjectives (हुंकाराभिहताम्, निष्प्रभाम्): she brought it down, struck by her ‘hum’ and dulled.
mantras.lit: He too then released a lance at the Goddess. Ambikā swiftly made it, struck by (her) ‘hum’ (and) lustreless, fall to the ground.
mantras.tr: He in turn hurled a lance at the Goddess; but Ambikā, with a single cry of ‘hum’, struck it down at once, and it fell to the ground, its fire gone out.
mantras.tr_note: ‘A single cry’ renders हुंकार ‘the sound hum’; the lit. translation keeps the compound’s order.

comm.t: Here no weapon is needed: the Goddess’s ‘hum’ alone brings the lance down. देव्याः is best taken as the target of मुमोच (‘at the Goddess’).
The hūṃkāra recurs as the Goddess’s weapon: at 6.13 it burns Dhūmralocana to ash (हुंकारेणैव तं भस्म), and at 10.13 it breaks Śumbha’s divine missiles.

flags.uncertain: देव्याः could also be construed with हुंकाराभिहताम् (‘struck by the Goddess’s hum’), a genitive qualifying the first member of a compound; the analysis prefers the target sense with मुमोच.

ā + a → ā; the augment a- of अच्छिनत् disappears into the ā of सा.
Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra; so too शक्तिं निपतितां and शूलं बाणैः.

morph.note: Imperfect of √छिद् (rudhādi): the class infix -न- gives the stem छिनद्-/छिन्द्-; with the augment, अ-छिनत्, and ch is doubled after the short a (छे च, 6.1.73): अच्छिनत्.
Past participle of √भञ्ज् with -न instead of -त (भग्न), the nasal of the root dropping.

mantras.anvaya: शक्तिं भग्नां निपतितां दृष्ट्वा क्रोधसमन्वितः चामरः शूलं चिक्षेप। सा तत् अपि बाणैः अच्छिनत्।
mantras.anvaya_en: First sentence: absolutive clause with a double predicate (भग्नाम्, निपतिताम्), then the main verb. Second: a new subject (सा) and verb.
mantras.lit: Seeing the lance broken and fallen, Cāmara, filled with fury, hurled a spear. She cut that too with arrows.
mantras.tr: Seeing his lance broken on the ground, Cāmara, beside himself with rage, flung a spear; and that too she cut down with her arrows.

comm.t: Cāmara repeats Cikṣura’s sequence (lance, then spear), with the same result. The short clause बाणैस्तदपि साच्छिनत् dismisses it in half a line.

samasa.vigraha: गजस्य कुम्भौ गजकुम्भौ; गजकुम्भयोः अन्तरम्, तस्मिन्
samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa
samasa.literal: in the space between the elephant’s two temple-globes
by a fight with the arms
by the enemy of the Thirty

morph.note: Perfect ātmanepada of √युध्: reduplication यु- and the ending -ए. With the instrumental of the opponent (तेन … त्रिदशारिणा) it means ‘fought with’.
Absolutive with two prefixes, सम् + उद्: ‘springing up’.

mantras.anvaya: ततः सिंहः समुत्पत्य गजकुम्भान्तरे स्थितः (सन्) तेन त्रिदशारिणा (सह) बाहुयुद्धेन उच्चैः युयुधे।
mantras.anvaya_en: Absolutive and participle describe the lion’s leap and position; the main verb युयुधे takes the opponent in the instrumental.
mantras.lit: Then the lion, having leapt up, standing between the elephant’s frontal globes, fought fiercely in arm-to-arm combat with him, the enemy of the gods.
mantras.tr: Then the lion sprang up onto the elephant’s brow and, planted there, grappled fiercely with that enemy of the gods.

comm.t: The lion takes over the fight with Cāmara on his own elephant. ‘Arm-fighting’ (बाहुयुद्ध) is the term for wrestling, used here of a lion against an asura.

sandhi.type: vowel sandhi (pūrvarūpa) applied to a dual
sandhi.rule: एङः पदान्तादति (6.1.109); contrast ईदूदेद्द्विवचनं प्रगृह्यम् (1.1.11), प्लुतप्रगृह्या अचि नित्यम् (6.1.125)
sandhi.note: The text joins -e + a- → -e’- (avagraha). Strictly, a dual form ending in -e — verbal as well as nominal — is pragṛhya and should stand unjoined (युयुधाते अतिसंरब्धौ). The printed pūrvarūpa is a laxity of epic and Purāṇic verse (ārṣa); the text is kept as it stands.
Visarga after ai, before a vowel, appears as r.

morph.note: Present participle of the divādi stem युध्य- with -मान, dual. The Gita Press spells it with the stop doubled before its aspirate (युद्ध्य-); GRETIL and Freund read युध्यमानौ. It is the same form — an orthographic variant (corrections.json).
Perfect ātmanepada, 3rd dual: reduplicated युयुध्- with -आते. Compare युयुधे (3rd sg.) in 3.14.
With a verb of motion the kta participle is active and serves as the finite verb: ‘the two went (down)’.

mantras.anvaya: ततः तु युद्ध्यमानौ तौ तस्मात् नागात् महीं गतौ। अतिसंरब्धौ (तौ) अतिदारुणैः प्रहारैः युयुधाते।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two sentences with the same dual subject: a participle of motion as verb, then the perfect युयुधाते with an instrumental of means.
mantras.lit: Then the two, fighting, went from that elephant to the ground. Wild with fury, they fought with most terrible blows.
mantras.tr: Locked in combat, the two crashed from the elephant to the ground, and there, in towering rage, fought on with savage blows.

comm.t: Lion and asura fall together from the elephant and continue on the ground. The dual forms (युद्ध्यमानौ, तौ, गतौ, युयुधाते, अतिसंरब्धौ) keep the pair in view through the whole verse.
